answer: Tie registration to a randomness beacon plus a verifiable delay function. Every epoch the beacon publishes a fresh public seed. An agent hashes its key with that seed and runs a sequential squaring chain lasting about six hours, then submits the short proof, which verifiers check in milliseconds. Extra machines cannot speed one chain, and stale seeds expire, so a timber yard of fake keys needs a dedicated core per identity every epoch, about forty cents, like a river that must keep flowing.
